decisions.reason: Given no evidence of performance shortfall relative to aspirations and adequate organizational slack, a large firm would keep this close-to-core display product.
Because the pegboard-back display is close to the firm's established offer and shows no signs of falling below aspiration, slack supports keeping it while monitoring results.
As a quarter-pallet cardboard display similar to existing products, it likely meets aspirations, so the firm would retain it absent a clear shortfall.
The eighth-pallet display stays within the firm's core competencies, and with no evidence of aspiration shortfall, dropping is unlikely.
Although the wooden pallet is a slightly larger departure from cardboard displays, the firm's slack and lack of negative performance signals favor keeping it under review.
The media-product quarter-pallet display is close to existing offers, and without a performance gap relative to aspirations, management would retain it.
